g.text: Flexible and user-friendly real-time closed-loop software
Open source, actively developed, and installed with a single command.
Closed-loop experiments causally infer the physiological role of transient neural events (such as replay
or ripples) by decoding brain states from real-time streaming data and triggering external feedback with
minimal latency. Falcon reads the acquisition system, runs a user-defined pipeline and drives the
stimulation. Its new engine is designed to do this for hundreds of channels at 30 kHz on a standard CPU.
Real-time path from sample to stimulus
users can add their own processors in C++
TTL output, saved streams and events
Each processing step runs on 16 channels
at once, using AVX-512 vector instructions.
Processors on the same CPU core exchange
data directly, without queues or waiting.
Samples are processed one at a time, as
soon as they arrive, not in packets.
Live viewer rendered on the GPU
The pipeline is assembled by drag and drop. Before each run,
it is translated to C++ and compiled.
A lightweight signal viewer. GPU compute shaders reduce 30 000
samples per second to screen resolution, with no load on the CPU.
x86 CPU with AVX2 or AVX-512
First described in D. Ciliberti and F. Kloosterman, J. Neural Eng. 14, 045004 (2017).
